explanation: Fires on an incomplete first piece of a word that the tokenizer splits. Two kinds: a German noun start right after an article ('eine[ We]ile', 'einen[ An]trag', 'einen[ Bet]rag'), and partial UTF-8 byte tokens of CJK/Japanese characters (the first byte fragment of a character, often after brackets or katakana). Whole English words barely activate it.

Fires on digits inside numbers, strongest on the version digit after a software name in Q&A titles ('Python [3].7', 'd[3].js', 'Rails [3]', 'XCode [3].1'). It is moderate on digits in coordinates, angles ('9[0] degrees') and stats, and weak on most other tokens. There are a few unrelated technical-token offshoots ('.org', 'resolver', 'FT-IR').

No clear single trigger. Strong hits are scattered content and function tokens, mostly in StackExchange-style technical questions ('on[ Windows]', '[ from] /home', '[ alloc]', 'an[ event] handler', '[ eclipse]', '[ IE]9'), plus some biomedical and dental terms and a football score. It seems to like key nouns/tokens in technical question titles and bodies, but it is not predictable.

Fires on a word-level token that completes a specific, recognizable named entity or API identifier: Python/Java/JS library and class names ('[ timedelta]', 'org[.hibernate]', '[ WebClient]', 'Object[.defineProperty]', '[ UIControl]', '$.[getJSON]', '</[tbody]>'), and proper names or brands ('Christie', 'Whatsapp', 'Brexit', 'San Diego'). It is weaker on ordinary content words.

Fires in source code at assignment statements, on the assignment operator or the start of the left-hand side, especially field/member assignments inside constructors or methods ('[ @]conversation =', 'self.run_time[ =]', '[ this].context =', 'logger[ =]', '@config[ ||=]', '$this[->]data'). Other code tokens activate it weakly, and prose barely at all.

Fires on tokens that are almost fully predictable from formulaic context. Mostly license boilerplate ('Licensed under the Apache[ License]', 'must reproduce[ the] above', 'MIT[ license]', 'data protection[ rights]'), plus templated math word problems ('What[ are] the prime factors'), stock code idioms ('type="[text]/javascript"', 'apply-[templates]') and stock question phrasings. Non-formulaic prose is weak.

Fires on the connective that follows a complete clause and introduces its purpose, result or continuation, usually after a comma: ', so (that)', 'hence', 'thus', infinitival 'to' meaning 'in order to', and clause-joining 'and'. It is strongest for 'so' after a clause describing a setup or action.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a rare or technical word that is split into pieces, most strongly when the fragment is 'g'/'G' ('[ G]DI', '[-g]ivers', '[ g]izmos', '[ g]allerists', '[ G]bE', '[G]y', '[ g]olang', '[ G]Parted'). Other word-initial fragments ('pr', 'fr', 'Intr', 'dec') activate it moderately. Whole common words do not.

Fires on a mid-word or final subword piece of a rare word or proper name split into several tokens, especially surnames and given names ('Bond[i]', 'Sam[mi]', 'Tymin[ski]', 'Naj[ib]', 'Yamas[aki]', 'Mi[key]') and technical words ('ax[on]', 'Dan[az]ol', 'unamb[igu]ously', 'disamb[ig]uation'). Common whole words are weak.

Fires on the word-initial subword fragment of a word split into pieces, mainly in non-English Latin-script text (Spanish/Portuguese/French/German/Czech/Norwegian: '[P]ero', '[ bus]quem', '[ p]obreza', '[ sup]prime', 'verall[geme]inernden'). It also fires on first fragments of rarer English or scientific words ('[ tre]asured', '[ c]uffed', 'therm[op]lastic'). Common whole English words are weak.

No coherent theme. Strong hits include C macro name pieces ('BOOST_SPIR[IT]'), 'PER CURI[AM]', the qmake '+=' operator, citation-ID digits ('ijerph-[1]7', 'JAHA.[1]17'), XML/meta attributes, and assorted prose function words ('the firm[ was]', 'most[ part]', 'you['ve]'). It mixes code identifiers, document IDs and prose.

A mixture: digits inside copyright year ranges ('2005-2[0]08'), the indentation whitespace token after '$.ajax({', fragments of foreign or rare proper names ('[ Man]asseh', 'Bh[ag]avatha', 'Zhu Sh[ij]ie', '[ Bul]ger', '[Al]fred'), Cyrillic word pieces and some code punctuation. There is no single predictable trigger.

Fires in text about synthetic chemicals, pesticides, toxins and drugs. Strongest on pieces of chemical compound names ("p,p['-]DDE", 'polychlor[inated]', '[ is]oxazoles', 'trich[lor]fon', 'CFCs') and moderately on function words in that context ('use[ of] insecticides', 'azoles[ and]', 'agents[ like]'). Non-chemistry text barely activates it.

Fires on the function word that completes a paired or comparative construction after an adverb/adjective, most often 'or'/'and' ('individually[ and]/[ or]', 'gradually[ or]', 'accidentally[ or]', 'rarely[ or] never', 'such[ as]', 'as casually[ as]', 'but[ also]'). It also fires on 'is' after a definitional subject phrase ('the easiest way to do this[ is]', 'one way to grasp NPV[ is]').
